name: Jean-Charles Naouri
current_role: President of Euris SAS (holding company); former chairman-CEO of Groupe Casino until March 2024
profile: French financier who left the civil service in 1987 to found investment holding Euris, then bought Rallye (1991) and used a layered holding structure to control retailer Groupe Casino from 1992. CEO of Casino until a 2024 debt restructuring handed control to Daniel Kretinsky's consortium and wiped out most of his stake.
interesting_fact: As chief of staff to finance minister Pierre Bérégovoy (1982-86), he is credited with France's 1984-86 financial-market reforms, including creation of the MATIF futures market and MONEP options market.
deep_cut_fact: He won first prize in Latin and Greek at the Concours général aged 14, got his baccalauréat at 15, and placed first in the 1967 École normale supérieure entrance exam; he is honorary president of the Institut de l'ENS.
notes: Lost control of Casino in March 2024 (https://esmmagazine.com/retail/french-retailer-casino-changes-leadership-team-as-boss-naouris-era-ends-262309). French Wikipedia reports a Jan 2026 Paris court conviction for private corruption and spreading false information, so check this before any outreach. Very private, with no personal public channels. Forbes listing is from 2015 and he is likely no longer a billionaire.

name: Laurent Burelle
current_role: Chairman of the Board, OPmobility SE (formerly Plastic Omnium); CEO of family holding Burelle SA
profile: Son of Plastic Omnium founder Pierre Burelle, he joined the family group in the mid-1970s, ran it as CEO from 2001 to 2019 and refocused it on automotive exterior systems and fuel tanks. Now non-executive chairman of OPmobility (renamed 2024), where daughter Félicie Burelle became CEO after Laurent Favre left in Nov 2025. He led French business lobby Afep from 2017 to 2023.
interesting_fact: Under his chairmanship Plastic Omnium was renamed OPmobility in 2024 and has invested in hydrogen mobility (tanks, fuel-cell systems) and electrification, which is relevant to an energy podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He started at the group's Langres plant around age 25 after initially planning to work for Alfa Laval, and at 28 moved to Spain to run the Valencia plant, becoming head of the Spanish subsidiary in 1980. He trained as a chemical engineer at ETH Zurich and MIT.
notes: Governance change Nov 2025: Félicie Burelle took over as CEO (https://www.opmobility.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/evolution-in-the-governance-of-opmobility-se-20251107-en.pdf). Best route is via OPmobility corporate communications. Wiki sources disagree on the exact chairmanship start date (2020 vs 2021).

name: Bruce Springsteen
current_role: Singer-songwriter; leader of the E Street Band (Land of Hope and Dreams American Tour, spring 2026)
profile: New Jersey rock musician who built a fortune over five decades of recording and touring with the E Street Band: more than 140 million albums sold, 20 Grammys, an Oscar and a special Tony. In 2021 he sold his recorded-music and publishing catalog to Sony for a reported ~$500M. He is still touring, with a 20-date US arena and stadium tour in spring 2026.
interesting_fact: He and the E Street Band came up playing Jersey Shore clubs, most famously Asbury Park's Stone Pony. His 2021 catalog sale to Sony was one of the largest ever for a single artist.
deep_cut_fact: His first known recording came in May 1966 with his teenage band the Castiles: a demo at Mr. Music in New Jersey, paid for by manager Tex Vinyard, of 'Baby I' and 'That's What You Get', co-written with George Theiss. 'Baby I' was finally released 50 years later on the 2016 album Chapter and Verse.

public_contacts.value: Shore Fire Media (Bruce Springsteen press page)

notes: Media requests go through his longtime publicist Shore Fire Media (Brooklyn). He rarely does business podcasts but did host the Renegades podcast with Barack Obama (Spotify, 2021). Sources disagree on where the 1966 demo was recorded (Toms River vs Bricktown).

name: Li Weiping
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Leadshine Intelligent Control Co. (002979.SZ)
profile: MIT-trained robotics PhD (born 1962) who left academia in 1997 to found Leadshine in Shenzhen. The company makes stepper/servo motors, drives and motion controllers for factory automation and listed on the Shenzhen exchange in 2020. He is the controlling shareholder alongside his wife, director Shi Huimin, and still runs the company as chairman and general manager.
interesting_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he was an associate professor at Washington State University (1991-94) and at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (1995-97).
deep_cut_fact: He is the 'Li' of 'Slotine & Li': he co-authored the classic textbook 'Applied Nonlinear Control' (1991) with MIT's Jean-Jacques Slotine, still a standard robotics/control text. He also wrote a Chinese book on motion-control system principles and applications.
notes: Chair of the 5th board, re-elected May 2023, and chaired board meetings through 2025. The textbook link (Slotine & Li) is a strong hook for a technical audience. The company is an automation/robotics play, adjacent to humanoid-robot supply chains.

name: Renichi Takenaka
profile: Ren'ichi Takenaka (1911-1996), 15th head of the Takenaka family and longtime president (from 1945) and later chairman (from 1980) of Takenaka Corporation, one of Japan's 'Big Five' general contractors. He died on 31 December 1996.
interesting_fact: A Waseda-trained architect, he won the Mainichi Industrial Technology Award (1975) for an energy-saving air-conditioning system, and Takenaka received the Deming Prize in 1988.
notes: Deceased (died 31 Dec 1996, per Japanese Wikipedia). His son Toichi Takenaka is honorary chairman of Takenaka Corporation (https://www.takenaka.co.jp/takenaka_e/about/message). The 1996 Forbes listing predates his death.

name: Charles Zhengyao Lu
current_role: Co-founder of Cotti Coffee (founded 2022); former chairman of Luckin Coffee and Car Inc.
profile: Fujian-born serial entrepreneur who founded rental-car firm Car Inc. (2007, HK IPO 2014) and ride-hailing UCAR, and was the angel backer and chairman of Luckin Coffee (Nasdaq IPO 2019). After Luckin's 2020 accounting scandal he was removed as chairman. In 2022 he and Qian Zhiya started rival chain Cotti Coffee, reported at about 15,000 stores by 2025.
interesting_fact: Cotti Coffee, his comeback venture, grew to about 15,000 stores in 28 countries within three years of its October 2022 launch.
deep_cut_fact: Born in 1969 in Pingnan County, Fujian, he studied industrial electrical automation at the University of Science and Technology Beijing (1991) and spent two years as a civil servant in Shijiazhuang before quitting in 1993 to start a business in Beijing's Zhongguancun tech district.
notes: Sensitive: the 2020 Luckin fraud led to a US$180M SEC penalty, a Beijing court ordered him to repay about CNY1.9B (yicaiglobal.com), and a Dec 2025 report says he lost control of his Luckin shares. He is probably no longer a billionaire. Very low public profile, with no personal channels found.

name: Jacques Nickolet
current_role: Co-founder and Supervisory Board member, Altarea (Altarea Cogedim); owner of OAK Racing / Ligier Automotive
profile: Jacques Nicolet (correct spelling; born 1956 in Gigondas) was development director at Pierre & Vacances (1984-94) before co-founding French property developer Altarea with Alain Taravella in 1994. Altarea bought Cogedim in 2007 and became one of France's largest developers. He long chaired Altarea's supervisory board and now sits on it, while running a motorsport business.
interesting_fact: A gentleman racer, he has driven at the Le Mans 24 Hours about ten times since 2007, and in 2012 founded Onroak Automotive, the race-car maker now known as Ligier Automotive.
deep_cut_fact: He won the 2010 1000 km of Zhuhai in China as a driver. His team OAK Racing grew out of Saulnier Racing, rebadged in 2009 as OAK Racing Mazda Team France.
notes: The input spells him 'Nickolet'; the correct name is Jacques Nicolet. Altarea's governance page lists him as a supervisory board member. The Le Mans/Ligier motorsport angle is the most natural hook. The Hurun listing is from 2014-15 and his wealth is shared with Alain Taravella.

name: Michael McCain
current_role: Executive Chair, Maple Leaf Foods and Executive Chair, Canada Packers Inc. (spun off Oct 2025)
profile: Son of McCain Foods co-founder Wallace McCain. He spent about 16 years at McCain Foods, rising to CEO of McCain Foods USA, then joined Maple Leaf Foods in 1995 when the family bought control. He was CEO from 1998/99 to May 2023 and is now executive chair. In October 2025 he led the spin-off of Maple Leaf's pork business as TSX-listed Canada Packers, which he also chairs.
interesting_fact: He championed Maple Leaf Foods becoming what it calls the world's first major carbon-neutral food company, in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: He led the creation of the Maple Leaf Centre for Food Security (founded late 2016), a charity tackling the systemic causes of food insecurity in Canada, and remains its honorary chair. He also sits on the board of the Daymark Foundation and is a CAMH Foundation trustee.
notes: Outspoken: he made headlines in 2020 for tweets about Trump's Iran policy after the PS752 crash, so he is comfortable with public commentary. The sustainability/carbon-neutral angle fits an energy podcast. The best route is Maple Leaf media relations.

name: Parakramsinh Jadeja
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, Jyoti CNC Automation Ltd (Rajkot, Gujarat)
profile: First-generation engineer-entrepreneur (P.G. Jadeja) who entered the machine-tool business in 1989 with Jyoti Enterprises and built Jyoti CNC into one of India's largest CNC machine makers, with 140,000+ machines installed in 60+ countries for defence, aerospace and auto customers. He listed the company in January 2024, making him a billionaire, and owns French 5-axis specialist Huron Graffenstaden.
interesting_fact: Jyoti was the first company to manufacture CNC machines in Gujarat. It owns Huron, a 160+-year-old French machine-tool maker known for 5-axis machining, with subsidiaries in France, Germany and Canada.
deep_cut_fact: Jadeja has described the company as 'A Temple of Technology', a vision written into the company history, and said it grew from a dream started in a small workshop. Jyoti says it made a 'tiny contribution' to the success of India's Mars Orbiter Mission.
notes: Also a director of the Indian Machine Tool Manufacturers' Association (IMTMA). Gives trade-press interviews (Machine Tools World, The Machinist), so manufacturing/industrial-automation angles are a natural fit. Spelled Prakramsinh/Parakram in some sources.

name: Sheela Gautam
profile: Founder of Sheela Foam (Sleepwell mattresses, founded 1971) and four-term BJP Lok Sabha MP for Aligarh (1991-2004). She died in New Delhi on 8 June 2019, aged 87. Her son Rahul Gautam runs Sheela Foam.
interesting_fact: She founded Sheela Foam in 1971 and also served four consecutive terms in parliament, from 1991 to 2004.
notes: Deceased (8 June 2019, per Wikipedia). For the company, contact Sheela Foam (sheelafoam.com), now run by son Rahul Gautam.

name: Zhang Jiangbo
current_role: Director and co-controlling shareholder, Ningbo Peacebird Fashion Co. (603877.SH)
profile: Ningbo-based co-founder of Peacebird, the Chinese apparel group led by his brother, chairman Zhang Jiangping, which has more than 4,000 stores across China. He sits on the board and is listed with his brother as actual controller, holding about 21% of the shares directly after 2023-24 internal transfers from Peacebird Group.
interesting_fact: In 1996 the brothers borrowed RMB 20,000 (about $2,900) to set up a garment factory with just six sewing machines, the start of the Peacebird fashion empire.
notes: Very low profile and overshadowed by his brother Zhang Jiangping, who is the public face. Board listing from a March 2025 SSE board resolution (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2025-03-28/1222923540.PDF). He was not in the April 2026 related-director list, so check his current board status. The best route is Peacebird corporate/IR.

name: Candido Pinheiro Koren de Lima
current_role: Founder and board member (former chairman), Hapvida NotreDame Intermédica, Brazil
profile: Oncologist from Ceará who used savings from his medical practice to open the Clínica (later Hospital) Antônio Prudente in Fortaleza in 1979. He added a health-plan business (Hapvida, 1993), took it public on the B3 in 2018 and merged it with NotreDame Intermédica, creating one of Brazil's largest health groups. His son Jorge was CEO for 24 years before moving to executive chairman in 2026.
interesting_fact: Hapvida started as a health insurer created mainly to generate income to sustain his hospital, and became the largest health plan operator in Brazil's North and Northeast.
deep_cut_fact: He named his first clinic after Antônio Prudente, founder of São Paulo's cancer-fighting association, and has said his original dream, his 'grande paixão', was an oncology-focused hospital. When HIV stigma was widespread, he chose to treat patients living with the virus. He is also an author ('Albuquerque. A Herança de Jerônimo').
notes: Aged about 80 (Forbes Brasil 2026: R$2.9B, https://forbes.com.br/listas/2026/09/quem-sao-os-13-bilionarios-brasileiros-no-setor-da-saude/). The 2026 leadership change (Jorge Pinheiro to executive chair, founder stays on the board) is reported at https://investidor10.com.br/noticias/hapvida-hapv3-anuncia-quem-assumira-em-2026-como-ceo-117584/, so check his exact title. Sources differ on the founding year (1979 vs 1986).

name: Hisakazu Yamaguchi
profile: Listed on Forbes' annual billionaires list in 1999-2000 with no source of wealth recorded. Searches in English and Japanese found no identifiable businessperson by this name.
notes: Could not identify. Possibly a romanisation variant of Hisakichi Yamaguchi, who appears on Forbes' 1991 and 1996 lists (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Japanese_people_by_net_worth), but that is unconfirmed. Low priority: last listed 2000.

name: Takao Katayama
profile: Appeared once on Forbes' annual billionaires list (2000) with no source of wealth recorded. A plausible but unconfirmed candidate is Takao Katayama, president of Union Tool Co. (TSE 6278, PCB micro-drill maker) from 1996 and chairman-CEO since 2014; Union Tool shares rose in the 2000 electronics boom.
notes: Identity not confirmed. The Union Tool candidate's current stake is worth well under $1B (MarketScreener estimates about $82M personally, with family holding company Koei owning about 31%: https://marketscreener.com/insider/TAKAO-KATAYAMA-A04WGF). Verify against the Forbes 2000 list before using.

name: Manoj Menda
current_role: Co-founder and Chair, Supervisory Board, RMZ (Bengaluru)
profile: Co-founded RMZ Corp in 2002 with his father Arjun and brother Raj, after the brothers spent years learning real estate at K Raheja Corp. RMZ became one of India's largest private office-park owners, sold 12.8M sq ft of offices to Brookfield for $2B in 2020, and is now a real-estate, infrastructure and private-capital group that is expanding into data centres through RMZ Digital Infrastructure.
interesting_fact: In 2020 RMZ sold 18% of its office assets (12.8M sq ft plus the CoWrks co-working business) to a Brookfield fund for $2B; Menda called it the firm's 'most important milestone' and said it made RMZ debt-free.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding RMZ, he and brother Raj spent several years at the Raheja group, where their father Arjun Menda had been part of its South India business. In 2023 the brothers received the Sindhi Chamber of Commerce Bangalore's Excellence in Business Award.
notes: Strong fit for a data-centre podcast: RMZ has a Digital Infrastructure unit and has said it is diversifying into data centres (aug-2023 press release). He is also active in WEF, YPO and ULI. Best route is RMZ's Head of PR.

name: Dong Xiang
current_role: Co-owner (with husband Dai Xuebin) of Lanrun Group (蓝润集团), Chengdu; specific executive title not found
profile: Dong Xiang is the wife of Lanrun Group founder Dai Xuebin, and the couple are listed jointly on the Hurun rich lists (2019-2023). Lanrun is a Sichuan conglomerate that started in property (founded 2007, HQ in Chengdu since 2009) and moved into agriculture and food, taking control of Shenzhen-listed Longda Meishi (龙大美食, ~29.9%) in 2019.
interesting_fact: The couple entered Hurun's global rich list as newcomers with a shared fortune of RMB 11 billion, built on Lanrun's property-to-agribusiness pivot.
notes: Very low profile, with almost no public information on her own role. Dai Xuebin is the public face. Lanrun faced a 2020 trust-product repayment extension (Jiemian), so wealth may have fallen; last on Hurun in 2023. Not a strong outreach target.
